Native check

You don't need to have read the book. Answer as many as you like.

Page 1 · 2 · 3 · 4

Maman (mother), Baba (father) and -jan (dear) are Persian words, kept in the book.

1 Mispronounced words

The mother in the book mispronounces some foreign words. Do these sound like believable mispronunciations?

freezel

= freezer

Ameroca

= America

Ayzheimer

= Alzheimer's

amublace

= ambulance

buldozel

= bulldozer

2 Persian sayings

Some Persian sayings and images are translated word for word. Does each one give you some sense of its meaning, or does it mean nothing to you?

Rain doesn't fall upward from the earth.

A good year is known from its spring.

Don't eat sorrow

my heart is rotting

My hand is short and union with you is far.

if I say it, my tongue burns; if I don't say it, the marrow of my bones burns

the meal will turn to snake venom for me

no bread is going to warm up for you

my family shoved me into the henhouse

the sugar cube jumps in my throat

peek into every last corner

words cost nothing; it's just hot air

he would surely fall from Negar's eyes

Just a harvest-time promise?

let me serve you the guts of friendship on a tray

all their body hair fell right out

don't get so worked up, or your milk will dry up

no one will call you mute if you don't fart

Eat the head of my dick

You dick-head eater

laughing at our beards and dicks

wandering the streets like this with your dick in your hand

no matter what dick lands on our heads

3 Children's words

Some children in the book get words wrong, the way small children do. Does each one sound like a child's mistake, not a typo?

It's marmal stone. Marmal means really expensive.

marmal = marble

It's called Tatanic.

Tatanic = Titanic

Baba, Baba, wiw you buy me dis big dolly?

a little girl

Yes, I wiw buy you a dolly.

her father copies her

4 Nicknames

The friends in the book give each other playful nicknames, often as wordplay. Does each one work as a nickname in your language?

Alain Dickon

a nickname for one of the friends: the actor Alain Delon's name, with part of it turned into a rude word for penis

Elder of the Tavern

a mock-grand title, taken from Hafez's poetry

Eldie

a pet form of "Elder of the Tavern"

Taverny, my Tavvy

pet forms made from "tavern"

Leopard Farid

for a daring, reckless friend

Is Arasteh a trimmed-down Araasteh?

araasteh = Persian for "neat"

Her Ladyship Ms. Armaaan

the surname Arman, drawn out to mock

Mister Curly-haired Schrödinger

a mock title for someone who can't make up his mind

5 Jokes and wordplay

These lines contain a joke or a play on words. Does each one work in your language?

That's just his factory setting.

messing things up is simply his nature

Forgiven. The whole boulevard is yours.

in Persian, "forgive" also means "give away"

until yesterday you said "ass." Now you've gone all civilized and say "donkey"?

teasing a boy for switching to a politer word

Pir-to-pir? … Eagle Eye says peer-to-peer; Taverny says Eldie-to-Eldie.

he hears "peer" as Persian pir, "elder", the root of his nickname

Last night I could hear you ruminating.

chewing at night, like a cow chewing cud

What the hell's wrong with you this time, getting it up at us, Alain Dickon?

double meaning: sitting up proudly, and an erection

What izer wasn't he?

the mother catches only the end of "womanizer"

The friend of the cousin of our brother-in-law's master craftsman who is the richest man in Tehran

a boy's running boast

Or you're dick-brai... well, you already were dick-brained, now you've become even more dick-brained.

the insult is cut off, then made worse

Yeah, all of us own factories. … We've got a bullshit factory.

all they produce is bullshit: they just talk nonsense

You fossil, you're a monument to stupidity and decline

a mocking insult

life is like a thousand-toman banknote: whichever side you look at, it smells of lentil rice.

an absurd quip

This is how I talk; you hear me speak, you think it's poetry.

a boy answers in a sing-song rhythm

Careful you don't crack, Mr. Dick.

he has just puffed out his chest

You're the biggest cow of all.

"cow" = a dull fool, said to a man

he always got such a kick out of working the word "aware" into that sentence twice.

"aware" used twice, playfully

the problem is with the receiver; the transmitter can't fix it.

the friend's poor eyesight is the "receiver"

I mean Alain Dickon. Diiick.

the rude part of the pun, drawn out

If you're Hooman, then I'm Susan.

the gentle name Hooman doesn't suit such a hairy man

The derivative? Meaning? Or the meaning of the derivative? Or the derivative of meaning?

mock-profound wordplay

God willing, may you always be araasteh.

a blessing that puns on the surname Arasteh; araasteh = "neat"

I can't see anything without my glasses, objectively.

the character's habit word, used everywhere

6 A line by Hafez

This line by the poet Hafez is written without a comma, so it can be read in two opposite ways:

The wine there is real no metaphor.

  • One way: the wine is real, not a metaphor.
  • The other way: the wine is not real, only a metaphor.

Can your version be read both ways?
